Stars Mexico: Hirving Lozano, Santiago Gimenez, Edson Alvarez, Guillermo Ochoa, Orbelin Pineda. Korea: Son Heung-min, Lee Kang-in, Kim Min-jae, Hwang Hee-chan, Hwang In-beom. lines.text: In twenty eighteen, the defending world champions came to defend their crown. Two teams sent them home. Tonight, those two teams meet.
It took both of them, ten days apart, to knock Germany out. Mexico struck first. South Korea finished the job. And in the stands sits the man who witnessed both.
Last time, we predicted Canada would edge Qatar two-one. Tonight: the two giant-killers who toppled a champion — facing each other.
Welcome back to WorldCup twenty-six Legends, episode thirty-one. Mexico versus South Korea. The three-time hosts... against the pride of Asia.
And stay with me — because the story that connects these two nations is one of the great World Cup secrets.
First, the history. And it is true. Russia, twenty eighteen. Germany, the defending champions, in their opening match against Mexico.
The thirty-fifth minute. Hirving Lozano. A goal so big it set off earthquake sensors back in Mexico City.
Mexico one, Germany nil. The champions were rattled. And ten days later, South Korea delivered the final blow.
Two goals in stoppage time. Germany, the world champions, knocked out in the group — for the first time since nineteen thirty-eight.
Two nations. One fallen giant. It took both of them to do it.
Mexico carry their own legend — the only country to host the World Cup three times. Nineteen seventy, eighty-six... and now.
But also a curse: seven World Cups in a row, knocked out in the round of sixteen. The fifth game they can never reach.
And South Korea? In two thousand two, on home soil, they beat Italy and Spain and reached the semifinals.
The greatest run any Asian nation has ever made at a World Cup. A summer that changed Korean football forever.
Two proud giant-killers, each chasing the next chapter of an extraordinary story.
Now, Mexico. Hirving Lozano — the man who felled the champions — still electric on the wing.
Santiago Gimenez leads the line. Edson Alvarez anchors the midfield. And Guillermo Ochoa, at a record sixth World Cup.
The green wave, roared on by the loudest support in the Americas.
But Korea have a superstar. Son Heung-min — captain, talisman, one of the finest forwards on the planet.
Lee Kang-in pulls the strings. Kim Min-jae is a wall at the back. This is Korea's strongest side in a generation.
So here is the duel. Mexican passion and pedigree... against the pace and pride of the kings of Asia.
Our prediction — built on Mexican depth, on home-continent energy, and on a Korea side that fears no champion. Watch.
Mexico start fast. Pineda slides it through, and Santiago Gimenez finishes low. One-nil, Mexico.
But you do not give Son Heung-min a yard. He drives inside and curls it home. One-all. Korea roar.
Then the old hero strikes. A cross, and Hirving Lozano rises to win it. Two-one.
Two-one at the whistle, in our story. Mexico edge it — but Korea walk off with their heads high.
Do you agree? Comment MEXICO if the hosts have too much. Comment KOREA if Son and the giant-killers strike again.
And that man in the stands? Legend number thirty-one: the Ghost of the Champions. He watched a world champion fall, twice.
He keeps a shirt from the summer the giants died. Tonight he came to see history echo. Collect him inside the game.
Which brings us to YOU. At WorldCup twenty-six dot world, pick three of the forty-eight nations — and every goal they score scores for you.
Free to play. Climb the leaderboard, just for fun. No prizes. Hit like, send this to a friend, and subscribe — the legends are only beginning.
